To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we introduce the model of dynamic privacy-preserving authentication of data structures (DPPADS), we propose an efficient, fully dynamic and privacy-preserving authenticated list, and we propose an efficient privacy-preserving authenticated order query mechanism. [1]
we introduce a formal DPPADS model, and provide an efficient, fully dynamic and privacy-preserving solution to it, and that the solution can be extended to a variety of data structures. [1]
we have developed a new dynamic privacy-preserving data structure model that can be used to build a number of applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient, fully dynamic and privacy-preserving authenticated lists, trees and posets. [1]
the design and analysis of efficient DPPADS that support the following functionalities.
the design and analysis of efficient, fully dynamic privacy-preserving authentication mechanisms. [1]
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a new dynamic privacy-preserving data structure model and a number of efficient, provably secure and privacy-preserv- ing mechanisms that allow querying member and order information stored in lists, binary trees, and posets of bounded depth.
we have proposed the first fully dynamic authenticated data structure that is secure against malicious clients and servers.
the DPPADS model provides a flexible and powerful framework for privacy-preserving data management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first DPPADS model, and efficient constructions of such structures that are based on the well-studied authenticated data structure (ADS) model.
we provide efficient and fully dynamic solutions for authenticated order queries on lists, trees, and posets. [1]
we provide the first fully dynamic privacy-preserving authentication mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that the problem can be solved efficiently in a dynamic setting for a variety of data structures.
we show how to efficiently implement DPPADS in the setting of authenticated data structures, and that this approach is applicable to a wide range of data structures.
the DPPADS model is a natural and general framework that can be used to model and solve several important practical problems in a privacy-preserving manner.
